statement: A non-listed company must hold its annual general meeting within 6 months after its financial year end; a private company need not hold an AGM if it sends its financial statements to all members within 5 months after the financial year end or qualifies as a dormant company, and may dispense with AGMs altogether by a resolution of all members, but AGM status must be declared in the annual return and a member may still demand an AGM up to 14 days before the six-month deadline.
caveat: Listed companies run on a four-month deadline, and extensions of time need an ACRA application before the deadline. The underlying provisions are Companies Act 1967 sections 175 and 175A; verify the statutory text and current guidance before relying.
